newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends Tokyo down ahead U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends Tokyo down ahead U.S. jobs data.

text.p: The benchmark June three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures contract on TIFFE ended Tokyo easier on Friday, mainly due to dealers' position adjustment ahead of October U.S. jobs data and the long weekend.
The U.S. jobs data is due at 1330 GMT.
Recoveries in Tokyo stocks also hurt Euroyen futures prices, traders said.
TIFFE will be closed on Monday for a national holiday.

The June price of 99.30 provided strong resistance for the market. Traders have challenged the resistance several times this week, but failed to breach the level, inviting position adjustment selling throughout the session on Friday.
Foreign speculators were content to stay on the sidelines.
The benchmark overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.46 percent, down from Thursday's 0.49 percent.

The fall in the call rate, which is typically observed at the beginning of the month, also reflected a projected fund surplus next week due to the expected return of cash in circulation to the market.
Activity in the September 1997 contract, turnover in which exceeded that in the June at one time this week, was slow on Friday, with traders wary of betting on either side, traders said.

"When the market mood is bullish, turnover in the September has tended to increase in line with the market belief that the Bank of Japan will not tighten its grip before the mid-next year," said another city bank trader.
However, in a bearish mood, such speculation did not intensify, resulting in limited turnover in the September, traders said.
The key three-month certificates of deposit were traded at 0.51 percent, unchanged from Thursday.
The Bank of Japan injected a net 200 billion yen into the money market through its regular operation at 0020 GMT to offset a projected 190 billion yen shortfall.
The operation was neutral to the market.
